module pe
(
    input clk,
    input rst,
    input [31:0] a,
    input [31:0] b,
    output reg [31:0] c
);

always @(posedge clk or posedge rst) begin
    if (rst) begin
        c <= 32'b0;
    end else begin
        c <= c + (a * b);
    end
end
endmodule

<module id="parallel2serial">
    <description>Parallel-to-Serial Conversion Module</description>
    <ports>
        <input id="clk">Clock signal for synchronous operation.</input>
        <input id="rst_n">Reset signal; active low.</input>
        <input id="d" width_description="[3:0]">4-bit parallel data input.</input>
        <output id="valid_out">Valid signal indicating the availability of serial output.</output>
        <output id="dout">Serial output representing the converted data.</output>
    </ports>
    <parameter_description>
        <!-- No parameter description needed for this module -->
    </parameter_description>
    <logic_description type="sequential_logic">
        <register id="cnt" width_description="[1:0]" initial_value="2'b00">
            <description>Counter register for tracking the current bit position during conversion.</description>
            <update_condition>On each clock edge.</update_condition>
            <update_expression>cnt + 1</update_expression>
        </register>
        <register id="data" width_description="[3:0]" initial_value="4'b0000">
            <description>Data register to hold the parallel data being converted.</description>
            <update_condition>When cnt reaches 3.</update_condition>
            <update_expression>d</update_expression>
        </register>
        <register id="valid" width_description="[0:0]" initial_value="1'b0">
            <description>Valid signal register to indicate the availability of serial output.</description>
            <update_condition>On each clock edge.</update_condition>
            <update_expression>valid ? 1'b0 : 1'b1</update_expression>
        </register>
    </logic_description>
    <implementation>
        // Assigning the most significant bit of the data register to the serial output
        assign dout = data[3];
        
        // Sequential logic for updating the data register based on the counter value
        always @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n) begin
            if (!rst_n) begin
                // Reset condition
                cnt <= 2'b00;
                data <= 4'b0000;
                valid <= 1'b0;
            end else begin
                if (cnt == 2'b11) begin
                    // Update data register with parallel input when cnt reaches 3
                    data <= d;
                    cnt <= 2'b00;
                    valid <= 1'b1;
                end else begin
                    // Increment counter and update valid signal
                    cnt <= cnt + 1;
                    valid <= 1'b0;
                    
                    // Shift data register left by 1 bit
                    data <= {data[2:0], data[3]};
                end
            end
        end
    </implementation>
</module>

    <description>Design an unsigned 16-bit multiplier using shift and accumulate operations.</description>
    <ports>
        <input id="clk">Chip clock signal.</input>
        <input id="rst_n">Active-low reset signal. Defined as 0 for chip reset and 1 for reset signal inactive.</input>
        <input id="start">Chip enable signal to initiate the multiplication operation.</input>
        <input id="ain" width_description="[15:0]">Input signal representing the multiplicand (a) with a data width of 16 bits.</input>
        <input id="bin" width_description="[15:0]">Input signal representing the multiplier (b) with a data width of 16 bits.</input>
        <output id="yout" width_description="[31:0]">Product output signal with a data width of 32 bits.</output>
        <output id="done">Chip output flag signal. Defined as 1 indicates the completion of the multiplication operation.</output>
    </ports>

    </parameter_description>

        <!-- Sequential logic description goes here -->
    </logic_description>
    <logic_description type="combinational_logic">
        <!-- Combinational logic description goes here -->
    </logic_description>
    <implementation>
        <!-- Detailed behavior description goes here -->
        Data bit control:
        On every positive edge of the clock signal (clk) or the falling edge of the reset signal (rst_n), the shift count register (i) is updated.
        If the reset signal (rst_n) is low, indicating a reset condition, the shift count register (i) is set to 0.
        If the start signal is active (start) and the shift count register (i) is less than 17, the shift count register (i) increments by 1.
        If the start signal is inactive (!start), the shift count register (i) is reset to 0.
        
        Multiplication completion flag generation:
        On every positive edge of the clock signal (clk) or the falling edge of the reset signal (rst_n), the multiplication completion flag (done_r) is updated.
        If the reset signal (rst_n) is low, the multiplication completion flag (done_r) is set to 0.
        If the shift count register (i) is equal to 16, indicating the completion of the multiplication operation, the multiplication completion flag (done_r) is set to 1.
        If the shift count register (i) is equal to 17, the multiplication completion flag (done_r) is reset to 0.
        
        Shift and accumulate operation:
        On every positive edge of the clock signal (clk) or the falling edge of the reset signal (rst_n), the module performs the shift and accumulate operation.
        If the reset signal (rst_n) is low, indicating a reset condition, the multiplicand register (areg), multiplier register (breg), and product register (yout_r) are reset to 0.
        If the start signal is active (start), the module starts the multiplication operation.
        When the shift count register (i) is 0, the multiplicand (ain) and multiplier (bin) are stored in the respective registers (areg and breg).
        For shift counts greater than 0 and less than 17, if the bit at position i-1 in the multiplicand register (areg) is high, the product register (yout_r) accumulates the shifted value of the multiplier register (breg) by shifting it left by i-1 positions and appending zeros at the least significant bit positions.
        
        Output assignment:
        The product output (yout) is assigned the value of the product register (yout_r).
    </implementation>

</module>

(
    input CLK,
    input RST,
    output reg [5:0] Hours,
    output reg [5:0] Mins,
    output reg [5:0] Secs
);

always @(posedge CLK or posedge RST) begin
    
    if (RST) begin
        
        Secs <= 6'd0;
    end else begin
        
        if (Secs == 6'd59) begin
            
            Secs <= 6'd0;
        end else begin
            
            Secs <= Secs + 1;
        end
    end
end

always @(posedge CLK or posedge RST) begin
    
    if (RST) begin
        
        Mins <= 6'd0;
    end else begin
        
        if ((Mins == 6'd59) && (Secs == 6'd59)) begin
            
            Mins <= 6'd0;
        end else if (Secs == 6'd59) begin
            
            Mins <= Mins + 1;
        end else begin
            
            Mins <= Mins;
        end
    end
end

always @(posedge CLK or posedge RST) begin
    
    if (RST) begin
        
        Hours <= 6'd0;
    end else begin
        
        if ((Hours == 6'd23) && (Mins == 6'd59) && (Secs == 6'd59)) begin
            
            Hours <= 6'd0;
        end else if ((Mins == 6'd59) && (Secs == 6'd59)) begin
            
            Hours <= Hours + 1;
        end else begin
            
            Hours <= Hours;
        end
    end
end

module signal_generator
(
    input clk,
    input rst_n,
    output reg [4:0] wave
);

reg [1:0] state;

always @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n) begin
    if (~rst_n) begin
        state <= 2'b00; 
        wave <= 5'b0;   
    end else begin
        case (state)
            2'b00: begin
                if (wave == 5'b11111) begin
                    state <= 2'b01; 
                end else begin
                    wave <= wave + 1; 
                end
            end
            2'b01: begin
                if (wave == 5'b00000) begin
                    state <= 2'b00; 
                end else begin
                    wave <= wave - 1; 
                end
            end
        endcase
    end
end
endmodule

module RAM
#(
    parameter WIDTH = 6,
    parameter DEPTH = 8
)
(
    input clk,
    input rst_n,
    input write_en,
    input [$clog2(DEPTH)-1:0] write_addr,
    input [WIDTH-1:0] write_data,
    input read_en,
    input [$clog2(DEPTH)-1:0] read_addr,
    output reg [WIDTH-1:0] read_data
);
	reg [DEPTH - 1 : 0] RAM [2**WIDTH-1:0];
	integer i;
	
	initial begin
		for(i = 0; i < 2**WIDTH; i=i+1) begin
			RAM[i] = 6'b000000;
		end
	end
	
	always @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n) begin
		if(!rst_n) begin
			for(i = 0; i < 2**WIDTH; i=i+1) begin
				RAM[i] <= 6'b000000;
			end
		end
		
		else if(write_en) begin
			RAM[write_addr] <= write_data;
		end
	end
	
	always @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n) begin
		if(!rst_n) begin
			read_data <= 6'b000000;
		end
		
		else if(read_en) begin
			read_data <= RAM[read_addr];
		end
		
		else begin
			read_data <= 6'b000000;
		end
	end
endmodule

<module id="synchronizer">
    <description>A multi-bit MUX-based synchronizer. Data remains constant during the period when data_en is high, and data_en is high for at least 3 clk_b clock cycles. The data change frequency of data_in is very low. The change interval between two adjacent data is at least 10 clk_b clock cycles.</description>
    <ports>
        <input id="clk_a">Clock signal A used for synchronous operations.</input>
        <input id="clk_b">Clock signal B used for synchronous operations.</input>
        <input id="arstn">Active-low reset signal A. Defined as 0 for reset and 1 for reset signal inactive.</input>
        <input id="brstn">Active-low reset signal B. Defined as 0 for reset and 1 for reset signal inactive.</input>
        <input id="data_in" width_description="[3:0]">Input data signal of size 4 bits.</input>
        <input id="data_en">Input enable signal that controls the selection operation.</input>
        <output id="dataout" width_description="[3:0]">Output data signal of size 4 bits.</output>
    </ports>
    <implementation>The module includes a register, data_reg, to store the input data signal, data_in. On the positive edge of clock signal A (clk_a) or the falling edge of reset signal A (arstn), the module updates the register. If the reset signal A (arstn) is low, indicating a reset condition, the register (data_reg) is set to 0. If the reset signal A (arstn) is high, the register (data_reg) is updated with the input data signal (data_in).</implementation>
    <task id="update_data_reg">
        <description>Update the data register based on the input data signal.</description>
        <input id="data_in" width_description="[3:0]">Input data signal of size 4 bits.</input>
        <output id="data_reg" width_description="[3:0]">Updated data register.</output>
    </task>
    <task id="update_en_data_reg">
        <description>Update the enable data register based on the input enable signal.</description>
        <input id="data_en">Input enable signal that controls the selection operation.</input>
        <output id="en_data_reg">Updated enable data register.</output>
    </task>
    <task id="update_en_clap_registers">
        <description>Update the enable clap registers based on the enable data register.</description>
        <input id="en_data_reg">Input enable data register.</input>
        <output id="en_clap_one">Updated enable clap one register.</output>
        <output id="en_clap_two">Updated enable clap two register.</output>
    </task>
    <task id="assign_output_data">
        <description>Assign the output data based on the enable clap registers.</description>
        <input id="en_clap_two">Enable clap two register.</input>
        <output id="dataout">Output data signal.</output>
    </task>
</module>

<module id="multi_pipe_8bit">
    <description>Unsigned 8-bit multiplier implemented using pipelined processing.</description>
    <ports>
        <input id="clk">Clock signal.</input>
        <input id="rst_n">Active-low reset signal.</input>
        <input id="mul_en_in">Input enable signal controlling multiplication operation.</input>
        <input id="mul_a" width_description="[7:0]">Multiplicand input with a data width of 8 bits.</input>
        <input id="mul_b" width_description="[7:0]">Multiplier input with a data width of 8 bits.</input>
        <output id="mul_en_out">Output enable signal indicating if multiplication operation is enabled.</output>
        <output id="mul_out" width_description="[15:0]">Product output with a data width of 16 bits.</output>
    </ports>
    <parameter_description>
        <!-- No parameter description needed for this module -->
    </parameter_description>
    <logic_description type="sequential_logic">
        <register id="mul_en_out_reg" width_description="[3:0]">Register to store the input enable signal.</register>
        <register id="mul_a_reg" width_description="[7:0]">Register to store the multiplicand input.</register>
        <register id="mul_b_reg" width_description="[7:0]">Register to store the multiplier input.</register>
        <register id="temp[0]" width_description="[15:0]">Register to store the first partial product.</register>
        <register id="temp[1]" width_description="[15:0]">Register to store the second partial product.</register>
        <register id="temp[2]" width_description="[15:0]">Register to store the third partial product.</register>
        <register id="temp[3]" width_description="[15:0]">Register to store the fourth partial product.</register>
        <register id="temp[4]" width_description="[15:0]">Register to store the fifth partial product.</register>
        <register id="temp[5]" width_description="[15:0]">Register to store the sixth partial product.</register>
        <register id="temp[6]" width_description="[15:0]">Register to store the seventh partial product.</register>
        <register id="temp[7]" width_description="[15:0]">Register to store the eighth partial product.</register>
        <register id="sum[0]" width_description="[15:0]">Register to store the first partial sum.</register>
        <register id="sum[1]" width_description="[15:0]">Register to store the second partial sum.</register>
        <register id="sum[2]" width_description="[15:0]">Register to store the third partial sum.</register>
        <register id="sum[3]" width_description="[15:0]">Register to store the fourth partial sum.</register>
        <register id="sum[4]" width_description="[15:0]">Register to store the fifth partial sum.</register>
        <register id="sum[5]" width_description="[15:0]">Register to store the sixth partial sum.</register>
        <register id="sum[6]" width_description="[15:0]">Register to store the seventh partial sum.</register>
        <register id="sum[7]" width_description="[15:0]">Register to store the eighth partial sum.</register>
        <register id="mul_out_reg" width_description="[15:0]">Register to store the final product.</register>
    </logic_description>
    <implementation>
        // Input control block
        always @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n) begin
            if (!rst_n) begin
                mul_en_out_reg <= 4'b0;
            end else begin
                mul_en_out_reg <= {mul_en_out_reg[2:0], mul_en_in};
            end
        end
        
        // Input registers
        always @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n) begin
            if (!rst_n) begin
                mul_a_reg <= 8'b0;
                mul_b_reg <= 8'b0;
            end else if (mul_en_in) begin
                mul_a_reg <= mul_a;
                mul_b_reg <= mul_b;
            end
        end
        // Partial product generation
        assign temp[0] = mul_b_reg[0] ? {{8{mul_a_reg[7]}}, mul_a_reg} : 16'b0;
        assign temp[1] = mul_b_reg[1] ? {{7{mul_a_reg[7]}}, mul_a_reg, 1'b0} : 16'b0;
        assign temp[2] = mul_b_reg[2] ? {{6{mul_a_reg[7]}}, mul_a_reg, 2'b0} : 16'b0;
        assign temp[3] = mul_b_reg[3] ? {{5{mul_a_reg[7]}}, mul_a_reg, 3'b0} : 16'b0;
        assign temp[4] = mul_b_reg[4] ? {{4{mul_a_reg[7]}}, mul_a_reg, 4'b0} : 16'b0;
        assign temp[5] = mul_b_reg[5] ? {{3{mul_a_reg[7]}}, mul_a_reg, 5'b0} : 16'b0;
        assign temp[6] = mul_b_reg[6] ? {{2{mul_a_reg[7]}}, mul_a_reg, 6'b0} : 16'b0;
        assign temp[7] = mul_b_reg[7] ? {{1{mul_a_reg[7]}}, mul_a_reg, 7'b0} : 16'b0;
        
        // Partial sum calculation
        always @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n) begin
            if (!rst_n) begin
                sum[0] <= 16'b0;
                sum[1] <= 16'b0;
                sum[2] <= 16'b0;
                sum[3] <= 16'b0;
                sum[4] <= 16'b0;
                sum[5] <= 16'b0;
                sum[6] <= 16'b0;
                sum[7] <= 16'b0;
            end else begin
                sum[0] <= temp[0];
                sum[1] <= temp[1] + temp[0];
                sum[2] <= temp[2] + temp[1] + temp[0];
                sum[3] <= temp[3] + temp[2] + temp[1] + temp[0];
                sum[4] <= temp[4] + temp[3] + temp[2] + temp[1] + temp[0];
                sum[5] <= temp[5] + temp[4] + temp[3] + temp[2] + temp[1] + temp[0];
                sum[6] <= temp[6] + temp[5] + temp[4] + temp[3] + temp[2] + temp[1] + temp[0];
                sum[7] <= temp[7] + temp[6] + temp[5] + temp[4] + temp[3] + temp[2] + temp[1] + temp[0];
            end
        end
        // Final product calculation
        always @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n) begin
            if (!rst_n) begin
                mul_out_reg <= 16'b0;
            end else begin
                mul_out_reg <= sum[0] + sum[1] + sum[2] + sum[3] + sum[4] + sum[5] + sum[6] + sum[7];
            end
        end
        // Output assignment
        assign mul_out = mul_en_out_reg[3] ? mul_out_reg : 16'b0;
    </implementation>
</module>

    <description>A 64-bit Johnson counter implemented using Verilog.</description>
    <ports>
        <input id="clk">Clock signal for synchronous operation.</input>
        <input id="rst_n">Active-low reset signal to initialize the counter.</input>
        <output id="Q" width_description="[63:0]">64-bit register representing the current count value.</output>
    </ports>
    <parameter_description>None</parameter_description>
    <logic_description type="combinational_logic"></logic_description>
    <implementation>
        Always block sensitive to the rising edge of clk and the falling edge of rst_n.
        On reset (when !rst_n == 1), assign Q = 0.
        Otherwise, check Q[0]:
            If Q[0] == 0, assign Q = {1'b1, Q[63:1]}.
            Else, assign Q = {1'b0, Q[63:1]}.
    </implementation>
    <task></task>
</module>

<module id="div_8bit">
    <description>Implement a simplified radix-2 divider on 8-bit signed or unsigned integers. and the inputs are two 8-bit operands. The module accepts a dividend and a divisor as inputs and provides a 16-bit result containing both the quotient and the remainder. The design supports both signed and unsigned division operations.</description>
    <ports>
        <input id="clk">Clock signal used for synchronous operation.</input>
        <input id="rst">The reset signal to initialize or reset the module.</input>
        <input id="sign">1-bit indicates if the operation is signed (1) or unsigned (0).</input>
        <input id="dividend" width_description="[7:0]">8-bit input signal representing the dividend for division.</input>
        <input id="divisor" width_description="[7:0]">8-bit input signal representing the divisor for division.</input>
        <input id="opn_valid">1-bit indicates that a valid operation request is present.</input>
        <input id="res_ready">1-bit indicates that the 16-bit output result has already been acknowledged.</input>
        <output id="res_valid">1-bit output signal indicating the result is valid and ready.</output>
        <output id="result" width_description="[15:0]">16-bit the output containing the remainder in the upper 8 bits and the quotient in the lower 8 bits.</output>
    </ports>
    <parameter_description>
        <parameter id="ADD">6'b100000</parameter>
        <parameter id="SUB">6'b100010</parameter>
        <parameter id="SLT">6'b101010</parameter>
        <parameter id="SLLV">6'b000100</parameter>
        <parameter id="SRLV">6'b000111</parameter>
        <parameter id="SRAV">6'b000111</parameter>
        <parameter id="LUI">6'b001111</parameter>
        <parameter id="JALR">6'b001001</parameter>
        <parameter id="JR">6'b001000</parameter>
        <parameter id="NOP">6'b000000</parameter>
    </parameter_description>
    <logic_description type="sequential_logic">
        <signal id="neg_divisor" width_description="[7:0]" type="reg">Register to store the negative value of the divisor.</signal>
        <signal id="start_cnt" type="reg">Register to indicate the start of the division process.</signal>
        <signal id="cnt" type="reg">Register to track the number of iterations performed during the division process.</signal>
        <signal id="sr" width_description="[15:0]" type="reg">Shift Register to hold the current value of the dividend being divided.</signal>
        <signal id="sub_result" width_description="[15:0]" type="wire">Wire to store the result of subtracting the divisor from the shift register.</signal>
        <signal id="carry_out" type="wire">Wire to store the carry-out value after subtraction.</signal>
        <signal id="mux_out" width_description="[15:0]" type="wire">Wire to store the output of the multiplexer.</signal>
        <signal id="abs_dividend" width_description="[7:0]" type="wire">Wire to store the absolute value of the dividend.</signal>
        <signal id="abs_divisor" width_description="[7:0]" type="wire">Wire to store the absolute value of the divisor.</signal>
    </logic_description>
    <implementation>
        // Initialize variables
        sr <= {8'b0, abs_dividend};
        neg_divisor <= ~abs_divisor + 1;
        cnt <= 1;
        start_cnt <= 1;
        res_valid <= 0;
        // Check for valid operation and reset conditions
        if (rst == 1'b1) begin
            res_valid <= 1'b0;
        end else if (cnt == 8 && start_cnt == 1) begin
            // Division completed
            cnt <= 0;
            start_cnt <= 0;
            sr[15:8] <= sr[15:8];
            sr[7:0] <= sr[7:0];
        end else if (start_cnt == 1) begin
            // Perform division operation
            sub_result = sr - neg_divisor;
            carry_out = sub_result[15];
            mux_out = (carry_out == 1) ? sub_result : {sr[15], sr[15:1]};
            sr <= {sr[14:0], 1'b0};
            cnt <= cnt + 1;
        end else if (res_valid == 1 && res_ready == 1) begin
            res_valid <= 1'b0;
        end else begin
            res_valid <= res_valid;
        end
    </implementation>
</module>

<module id="alu">
    <description>ALU for a 32-bit MIPS-ISA CPU.</description>
    <ports>
        <input id="a" width_description="[31:0]">First operand.</input>
        <input id="b" width_description="[31:0]">Second operand.</input>
        <input id="aluc" width_description="[5:0]">Control signal for ALU operation.</input>
        <output id="r" width_description="[31:0]">Result of ALU operation.</output>
        <output id="zero">Zero flag.</output>
        <output id="carry">Carry flag.</output>
        <output id="negative">Negative flag.</output>
        <output id="overflow">Overflow flag.</output>
        <output id="flag">Flag for SLT and SLTU operations.</output>
    </ports>
    <parameter_description>
        <parameter id="ADD">6'b100000</parameter>
        <parameter id="ADDU">6'b100001</parameter>
        <parameter id="SUB">6'b100010</parameter>
        <parameter id="SUBU">6'b100011</parameter>
        <parameter id="AND">6'b100100</parameter>
        <parameter id="OR">6'b100101</parameter>
        <parameter id="XOR">6'b100110</parameter>
        <parameter id="NOR">6'b100111</parameter>
        <parameter id="SLT">6'b101010</parameter>
        <parameter id="SLTU">6'b101011</parameter>
        <parameter id="SLL">6'b000000</parameter>
        <parameter id="SRL">6'b000010</parameter>
        <parameter id="SRA">6'b000011</parameter>
        <parameter id="SLLV">6'b000100</parameter>
        <parameter id="SRLV">6'b000110</parameter>
        <parameter id="SRAV">6'b000111</parameter>
        <parameter id="LUI">6'b001111</parameter>
    </parameter_description>
    <logic_description type="combinational_logic">
        <assign id="signed_a" width_description="[31:0]">Signed version of a.</assign>
        <assign id="signed_b" width_description="[31:0]">Signed version of b.</assign>
        <assign id="res" width_description="[32:0]">Register to store the result.</assign>
        <assign id="shift_amount" width_description="[4:0]">Shift amount for shift operations.</assign>
        <always_comb>
            // Assigning values to signed_a and signed_b
            assign signed_a = $signed(a);
            assign signed_b = $signed(b);
            
            // Assigning the lower 32 bits of res to r
            assign r = res[31:0];
            
            // Setting flag based on aluc
            assign flag = (aluc == 6'b101010 || aluc == 6'b101011) ? 1'b1 : 1'bz;
            
            // Setting zero based on the result
            assign zero = (r == 32'h00000000) ? 1'b1 : 1'b0;
            
            // Setting carry based on the result
            assign carry = (r[32]) ? 1'b1 : 1'b0;
            
            // Setting negative based on the result
            assign negative = (r[31]) ? 1'b1 : 1'b0;
            
            // Setting overflow based on the result
            assign overflow = ((signed_a[31] && signed_b[31] && !r[31]) || (!signed_a[31] && !signed_b[31] && r[31])) ? 1'b1 : 1'b0;
        endalways_comb>
        
        // Always block for performing ALU operations
        always @(aluc, a, b) begin
            case(aluc)
                6'b100000: res <= signed_a + signed_b; // ADD
                6'b100001: res <= a + b; // ADDU
                6'b100010: res <= signed_a - signed_b; // SUB
                6'b100011: res <= a - b; // SUBU
                6'b100100: res <= a & b; // AND
                6'b100101: res <= a | b; // OR
                6'b100110: res <= a ^ b; // XOR
                6'b100111: res <= ~(a | b); // NOR
                6'b101010: res <= (signed_a < signed_b) ? 1 : 0; // SLT
                6'b101011: res <= (a < b) ? 1 : 0; // SLTU
                6'b000000: res <= {a[29:0], 2'b00}; // SLL
                6'b000010: res <= {2'b00, a[31:2]}; // SRL
                6'b000011: res <= {a[31], a[31:2]}; // SRA
                6'b000100: res <= {a[29:0], 2'b00} << a[4:0]; // SLLV
                6'b000110: res <= {2'b00, a[31:2]} >> a[4:0]; // SRLV
                6'b000111: res <= {a[31], a[31:2]} >>> a[4:0]; // SRAV
                6'b001111: res <= {a[15:0], 16'b0000000000000000}; // LUI
                default: res <= 32'hz; // Default case
            endcase
        end
    </logic_description>
    
    <implementation>Implements the ALU functionality described above.</implementation>
</module>
